newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL secondaries may rise more, blue chips mixed.
newsitem.headline: KL secondaries may rise more, blue chips mixed.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur secondary issues could extend their run-up on interest in selective stocks and positive retail sentiment, dealers said.

Meanwhile, the outlook for blue chips is more mixed. On Monday, the blue chip-focused Composite Index dropped 10.86 points to 1,162.09. The Second Board index, however, raced to a record at 637.10, up 10.86 points.
"The Second Board is filled with a lot of high-tech stocks which will keep things running," said Ralph Dixon, of TA Securities' international division. Overnight, the Dow slid 34 points.
"I think the Second Board will still be volatile, and the Composite Index should be pretty much flat," said Tony Shue, vice president of institutional sales at Jupiter Securities.

Among stocks in the news, dealers said a news conference scheduled to be held at 5 p.m. on Tuesday by infrastructure and power concern YTL raised speculation the firm would announce a deal with Hong Kong's Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd.
Shares of Tongkah and Faber may rise after the companies were among three named to receive a 7.5 billion ringgit Malaysian hospital support services contract, dealers said.
